🇺🇸 AMERICA'S FIRST SILVER DOLLAR SOLD FOR $10 MILLION

On October 15, 1794, the Philadelphia Mint delivered 1,758 silver dollars, struck on a hand-turned screw press. It was the only day of dollar production that year.

These Flowing Hair dollars were the first silver dollars issued by the United States. Fewer than 200 are believed to survive.

The finest known example is unusual. A small silver plug was added to its blank at the Mint to bring it up to standard weight, and some experts believe it may be the very first silver dollar struck.

In 1947 the coin changed hands for $1,250. On January 24, 2013, at a Stack's Bowers Galleries auction in New York, it sold for $10,016,875. It was the first coin ever to top $10 million at auction.
